title: Factory drill adapter protocol
description: Messages exchanged between a drill driver and a factory adapter. Transport is JSON over stdio, one message per line: the driver writes one command object per line and the adapter answers with exactly one observation object per line, in order. A message is valid when it matches either the command shape or the observation shape.

command.description: One instruction from the driver to the adapter. The op field selects the operation; params carries op-specific arguments.

oneOf.description: seed: load a scenario into the factory. After a successful seed the factory holds exactly the scenario's initial state and no execution has started. The mode selects the wiring under test: protected wires the safety mechanism (dedup destination, fenced publisher, session reattach, reconciler), unsafe wires the negative control that the oracle is expected to catch.

scenario.description: Drill scenario name, for example worker-dies-agent-survives.

mode.description: protected exercises the safety mechanism; unsafe is the negative control whose violation the oracle must detect.

oneOf.description: start: begin execution of the seeded scenario. Marks the run as started at the current logical tick; scenario steps advance only inside wait_for_barrier, so the driver controls exactly how far execution proceeds.

wait_for_barrier: run the scenario until the named barrier fires, then pause with the system frozen at exactly that point. Barriers are named causal points in the scenario, not delays; on success every step before the barrier has run and no step after it has. The terminal barrier is named run-complete.

name.description: Barrier name to run to. Reaching an earlier barrier on the way records it in coverage but does not pause.

oneOf.description: inject_fault: apply a fault while the run is paused at at_barrier, which must equal the barrier the run is currently paused at. This ties the fault to a position in the causal order rather than to timing. kill_worker terminates the worker process abruptly; sessions it launched survive it. drop_event arms the event bus to drop the next emitted event. expire_lease invalidates the current lease on the work item. drift_resource moves the named resource out of the state a later guarded write requires, leaving it otherwise intact.

at_barrier.description: Name of the barrier the run must currently be paused at.

target.description: Optional explicit target (worker id, work id, resource id); the adapter infers the scenario's default target when absent.

oneOf.description: advance_generation: allocate the next monotonic ownership generation for the work item, with a fresh lease. Models a successor writer taking ownership; the returned generation is strictly greater than every earlier generation for that work item.

read_authoritative_state: return the application ledger as the application believes it: work items (status, generation, lease), claims and the sessions bound to them, sessions, and effect records. This view can be stale relative to the destination; that gap is what some drills measure.

read_external_effects: return ground truth at the external destination: the ordered mutation list (with effect ids and receipts) and the currently published artifact. Must be read from the destination itself, never derived from the ledger.
read_running_executors: return the workers and sessions that are currently alive. A session can outlive the worker that launched it, so the two lists are reported independently.
read_campaign_coverage: return what this run has exercised so far: scenario, mode, the ordered list of barriers reached, the faults injected, and whether the run reached the run-complete barrier.

collect_evidence: return the full evidence record for the run: scenario, mode, barriers reached, faults, the ordered per-tick event log, the identity mappings (work, generation, attempt, session, worker, effect, artifact), and snapshots of the ledger, the destination, and the running executors.

observation.description: One reply from the adapter to the driver. ok reports whether the op succeeded; data carries the op-specific result; error carries a diagnostic when ok is false.

data.description: Op-specific result payload; present when ok is true.

error.description: Diagnostic message; required when ok is false.

else.description: A successful observation carries its result in data and no error field.
